newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sumitomo Bank aims for NYSE listing by 2000 - papers.
newsitem.headline: Sumitomo Bank aims for NYSE listing by 2000 - papers.

text.p: Sumitomo Bank Ltd hopes to list its shares on the New York Stock Exchange by 2000 as part of an effort to meet global business standards, major Japanese newspapers reported on Wednesday.
A Sumitomo spokeswoman, however, said that while the bank is considering such listing it has not decided on a date.

The spokeswoman said the bank aims to raise its capital adequacy ratio, as defined by the Bank for International Settlements, to 10 percent from the current 8.75 percent and to raise its return-on-equity to seven percent from the current two percent within three to five years.
Other Japanese banks such as Sanwa Bank Ltd and the Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd have also said they are interested in a NYSE listing.
To list shares on the New York bourse, companies are required to have posted profits for at least three years in a row immediately before the listing.
Sumitomo posted a parent current loss of 335.7 billion yen in the year to March 1995.
